official.status_note: Application period runs from 13:00 JST on 1 October 2026 to 13:00 JST on 31 October 2026 for both April and fall (September/October) 2027 enrolment; selection results are notified by email by mid-March 2027 and letters of acceptance are issued by the end of March 2027.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of 100,000 yen for undergraduates and 140,000 yen per month for master's students and doctoral students
Supplemental Payment for Travel Expenses to Japan of up to 250,000 yen, reimbursed against receipts after arrival and provided through the Sewa Club
Scholarship period of two years: April 2027-March 2029 for April enrolment, or September 2027-August 2029 / October 2027-September 2029 for fall enrolment
Personal support from Sewa Clubs and counselors after arrival in Japan
eligibility: International student scheduled to enrol in or transfer to a university or graduate school in Japan under the jurisdiction of MEXT in April, September, or October 2027, enrolled in a full-time degree programme
Must hold citizenship of a country other than Japan, enter Japan for study with 'Student' status of residence, and in principle reside outside Japan until enrolment
Must have passed the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test (JLPT) at N3 or above at the time of application (N2 or above encouraged)
Must be under 45 years of age as of 1 April of the award year (born on or after 2 April 1982)

In principle must not have stayed in Japan before the month scholarship payments begin, unless total stay before 1 October 2026 does not exceed 365 days, the stay was for family reasons until completion of compulsory education, or the applicant is a ROTEX alumnus

Research students, non-degree students, trainees, short-term international students, language schools, junior colleges, vocational schools, technical colleges and preparatory courses are not eligible; former Yoneyama Scholars and applicants to another Yoneyama programme are not eligible; concurrent receipt of the MEXT international-student promotion scholarship is prohibited
requirements: Register on the Foundation's website, enter information in the dedicated online forms and upload all application documents during the application period
Submit a complete set of documents for each university or graduate school applied to; applications with incomplete information are not accepted
Application documents must be prepared in either Japanese or English; the intended institution, course, faculty, graduate school and month of admission may not be changed after the deadline
Successful applicants must arrive in Japan by the designated arrival date (31 March / 31 August / 30 September 2027) and attend the district orientation, or eligibility is lost
If the admission decision is announced after the deadline, the letter of acceptance or admission permit must be submitted by 25 March 2027 (April enrolment) or 25 August 2027 (fall enrolment)
documents: Application Form (designated form with a front-facing 4.0 cm x 3.0 cm photograph taken within the last three months and a handwritten signature)
Research Proposal (designated form; required of all applicants including undergraduates; use of generative AI is prohibited)
Short Essay: 'Why did you choose Japan as your study destination, and what are your future plans after completing your studies in Japan?' (designated form; generative AI not permitted)
Letter of Recommendation (prescribed form, one page, with the recommender's handwritten signature; graduate applicants: from the prospective academic advisor at the intended institution)
Copy of the JLPT result notification showing N3 or above; a copy of any English-language proficiency test result is not required

Copy of the Letter of Acceptance or Admission Permit from the intended institution in Japan, or at application time a copy of that institution's application form or examination admission ticket plus its admissions guidelines
selection_criteria: Document screening by the Rotary Yoneyama Selection Committee of the district in which the prospective university is located; online interviews and contacts with the applicant or academic supervisor may be conducted
Applications with incomplete information or missing required documents are not considered for screening
Qualifications require enthusiasm and excellence in Academic Work, Cross-cultural Understanding, and Communication Skills
coverage: Monthly scholarship: 100,000 yen for undergraduates; 140,000 yen for master's and doctoral students

Travel to Japan up to 250,000 yen: one-way economy-class airline ticket, transportation expenses in the home country and within Japan, visa application fees, and first-day accommodation in Japan up to 10,000 yen
application_method: Online: download the designated forms from the Foundation website, register, enter information in the dedicated online forms and upload the documents
Apply to the intended Japanese university or graduate school independently and keep a copy of that admission application or examination admission ticket for the scholarship file
The Foundation emails the application receipt number; once all documents are uploaded the application is complete
official.application_route: Register on the Foundation's website and upload the full document set through the dedicated online forms, having already applied (or booked an entrance examination) at the intended Japanese university or graduate school.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of a country other than Japan; 'Student' status of residence on entry; in principle resident outside Japan until enrolment and no prior stay in Japan before the payment-start month (with the 365-day, family-reason and ROTEX exceptions)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to overseas (non-Japanese) nationals only; Japanese citizens are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of study are eligible; the institution must be a university or graduate school under MEXT jurisdiction (not junior colleges, vocational schools, technical colleges or preparatory courses)
official.research_requirement: A Research Proposal on the designated form is required of all applicants, including undergraduates (study plan for undergraduates; proposed research plan or research progress for graduate applicants); use of generative AI is prohibited
official.duration: Two years (April 2027-March 2029 for April enrolment; September 2027-August 2029 or October 2027-September 2029 for fall enrolment)
official.description: The Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Scholarship (Overseas Candidates) is a non-repayable scholarship funded by donations from Rotarians throughout Japan for overseas students scheduled to enrol in a Japanese university or graduate school, combining a monthly stipend and a travel-expense subsidy with personal support through Sewa Clubs and counselors.
official.program_type: Foundation scholarship - monthly stipend plus travel subsidy
official.english_requirement: No English-language proficiency test result is required; application documents must be prepared in either Japanese or English

not_confirmed: tuition coverage terms - the official pages publish only the monthly stipend and the travel subsidy and state no tuition benefit
verification.notes: Stipend tiers, travel subsidy, 1-31 October 2026 window, JLPT N3 rule, age limit, two-year scholarship period, eight-document list, selection process, arrival dates and post-result deadlines were all read directly from the Foundation's overseas-candidates page and the FY2027 Application Guide PDF (16 pages); the English guide notes the Japanese version prevails in case of discrepancy.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a living stipend, not a full scholarship - you will still fund tuition, admission fees and most living costs yourself. Undergraduates receive JPY 100,000 per month and master's or doctoral students JPY 140,000, plus up to JPY 250,000 back for flights, transport, visa fees and a first night in Japan once receipts are submitted. You need a JLPT N3 pass (N2 preferred) in hand and a named target university or graduate school before the one-month window opens, because the application form must state that exact institution. Winning carries real obligations - monthly Sewa Club meetings, Japanese-language reports twice a year and club speeches - so treat it as a community commitment as much as money.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funding-capable students with a JLPT N3+ pass, a concrete plan at a specific Japanese university, and appetite for Rotary community involvement.
application_readiness_checklist: Pass JLPT N3 (aim for N2) before applying - the result notification copy is mandatory and no English test substitutes for it
Apply to your target Japanese university or graduate school in parallel and keep copies of that admission application, examination admission ticket and admissions guidelines
Download the five designated forms from the Foundation's website and complete them in Japanese or English; no generative AI in the research proposal or essay
Secure a one-page recommendation letter with a handwritten signature (graduate applicants: prospective academic advisor); self or family-written letters are refused
Register early in October and upload everything before 13:00 JST on 31 October 2026, then watch for the receipt-number email
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete forms or missing documents are not screened at all - there is no chance to fix gaps
A vague or wrong institution entry (missing admissions-office contact details) makes the application void
Losing admission at the target university after winning revokes eligibility at that point
Holding the MEXT international-student promotion scholarship or other support above JPY 576,000 per year alongside Yoneyama forces repayment of the overlap
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, admission fees and the bulk of living costs; the award is a JPY 100,000-140,000 monthly stipend with only travel costs subsidised (capped at JPY 250,000: one-way economy airfare, public transport, visa fees, first-night stay up to JPY 10,000).
document_audit: The photo must be a recent (within three months), unedited 4.0 x 3.0 cm upper-body image - digitally altered pictures are rejected
A recommendation letter without the recommender's handwritten signature, or written by the applicant or a family member, is not accepted

If your admission letter arrives after the deadline you must still file it by 25 March 2027 (April enrolment) or 25 August 2027 (fall enrolment); an admission permit naming only a prospective advisor is not accepted
Every additional university you target needs its own complete set of documents
alerts: The window opens and closes at 13:00 JST sharp on 1 and 31 October 2026 - late uploads are not accepted
Count your days in Japan: stays before 1 October 2026 exceeding 365 days make you ineligible unless the narrow exceptions apply
You must land in Japan by the last day of the month before enrolment (31 March / 31 August / 30 September 2027) and attend the district orientation, or the award lapses
Age limit: under 45 on 1 April 2027 (born on or after 2 April 1982)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the Foundation's site, complete the dedicated online forms, upload the full document set and await the receipt-number email; screening then sits with the district Rotary committee where your target university is located, with possible online interviews.

official.deadline_central_display: 23 April 2027, 5 p.m. JST (FY2027 2nd recruitment, submitted from the host institution to JSPS)
official.deadline_note: Host institutions set their own internal deadlines, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline; the FY2027 1st recruitment deadline of 28 August 2026 has already passed.
official.application_cycle: FY2027 2nd recruitment (two recruitments per fiscal year)
official.status_note: FY2027 1st recruitment closed on 28 August 2026 (results late December 2026, 120 fellowships); FY2027 2nd recruitment deadline is 23 April 2027, 5 p.m. JST, with results in early August 2027, arrival windows 1 September - 30 November 2027 and 120 fellowships awarded.
benefits: Maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month
A round-trip air ticket based on JSPS's regulations
A settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 and overseas travel insurance
A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Research Fellow) to cover cooperative research-related expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
For candidates living in Japan (with a mailing address) before the fellowship starting date, the outbound airfare and the settling-in allowance will not be paid
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (JSPS treats Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers in this manner)

As of 1 April of the fiscal year, have obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect (on or after 2 April, six years prior to the fiscal year), or be expected to receive a Ph.D. by the fellowship start date
Researchers who obtained their PhD within six years minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks of leave counted as one month, remaining weeks also counted as one month)

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship Program for Research in Japan (Standard, and Pathway to University positions in Japan) are not eligible
Japanese citizens and foreigners permitted permanent residence in Japan are not eligible
The host researcher must be a full-time researcher affiliated with a KAKENHI-eligible institution, eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant; each host researcher can submit up to three applications
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
The application form must be submitted through the JSPS Electronic Application System by the deadline designated by the host institution
The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before the JSPS application period
Before transmitting the application, the host institution must verify that it has been approved by the head of the institution and that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved
The Letter of Recommendation must be filled out by the recommender of the foreign candidate within one page, written in English or in Japanese
documents: FORM1 (Reference): application form for the JSPS Electronic Application System, completed by the host researcher
FORM2: application form completed by the foreign candidate
Letter of Recommendation (Sample): filled out by the recommender of the foreign candidate within one page, written in English or in Japanese
selection_criteria: Selection by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers, through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second

Document reviews are conducted by six examiners per application, scored on a 1-5 scale, taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity, future potential of the research, and establishment of new research networks

Selection policy: the host-candidate collaboration must contribute to advancing science in Japan and other countries and advance the subject research; the applicant and candidate must have established contact in advance and created a concrete research plan; the host institution must establish a suitable place for the candidate to work and stay

Balance is sought across selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialization; reviewers with potential conflicts of interest are removed and all committee members comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month
Round-trip air ticket based on JSPS's regulations
Settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 and overseas travel insurance
Cooperative research-related expenses through a Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Research Fellow), applied for by the host researcher through their institution
application_method: Secure an eligible host researcher and host institution in Japan (JSPS does not introduce host institutions to applicants) and confirm the institution's internal deadline
The candidate completes FORM2 and obtains a one-page letter of recommendation; the host researcher enters and submits the application on the JSPS Electronic Application System
The host institution verifies the application and transmits it to the president of JSPS by the JSPS deadline
official.application_route: Applied for by the Japanese host researcher through the JSPS Electronic Application System via the host institution - overseas candidates cannot apply directly.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers treated in this manner); Japanese citizens and foreigners with permanent residence in Japan are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the fellowship is for young overseas researchers; Japanese citizens and permanent residents of Japan are excluded
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences
official.research_requirement: Conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher; the host and candidate must have established contact in advance and created a concrete research plan
official.description: The JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard) provides an opportunity for young overseas researchers to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of their hosts at universities and other research institutions in Japan, selected through Open Calls and Nominations.

not_confirmed: English language proficiency requirement - no IELTS/TOEFL or MOI rule is published; the recommendation letter is simply written in English or Japanese
study mode for fellows - not stated on the official pages
verification.notes: Maintenance allowance (JPY362,000/month), airfare, settling-in allowance (JPY200,000), overseas travel insurance, Grant-in-Aid option, 12-24 month duration, candidate and host eligibility rules, FY2027 recruitment deadlines and fellowship counts, and the two-stage selection process were all read directly from JSPS's Standard Program pages.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply yourself - a Japanese host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution submits the application through their university, so the first task is securing a host, since JSPS does not introduce hosts. Support is JPY 362,000 per month plus round-trip airfare, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance for 12-24 months, and the host can apply for a Grant-in-Aid for cooperative research expenses. Watch the internal deadline: institutions often close more than a month before JSPS's 23 April 2027 (FY2027 2nd) date, and the application system opens only about two months before. Hard gates to self-check first: the six-year PhD clock (less maternity/parental leave), no prior Standard or Pathway fellowship, and no Japanese citizenship or permanent residency.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers within six years of their PhD who already have, or can quickly build, a working relationship with a prospective host researcher in Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify and email prospective hosts months ahead - ask each institution for its own internal cut-off, which can fall more than a month before the JSPS deadline
Have your PhD certificate ready (expected-award evidence at application); selected fellows must submit the certificate or diploma before the fellowship start date
Complete FORM2 and secure a one-page recommendation letter in English or Japanese from your recommender
Agree a concrete research plan with your host in advance - the selection policy explicitly requires prior contact and a written plan
Confirm you have never held a JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship (Standard or Pathway) and that you hold no Japanese citizenship or permanent residency
common_rejection_risks: Cold applications with no established host relationship - the selection policy requires the pair to have made contact and drafted a concrete research plan
Missing the host institution's internal deadline while aiming at the JSPS date
A host at an institution that is not KAKENHI-eligible, or a non-full-time host without institutional backing
Falling outside the six-year PhD window without correctly deducting maternity and parental leave time
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing and day-to-day living costs beyond the JPY 362,000 monthly allowance; the fellowship is a fixed stipend, not a cost-of-attendance package, and carries no tuition benefit because fellows are research appointees rather than students.
document_audit: The recommendation letter must fit within one page and be written in English or Japanese - an overlength or wrong-language letter risks failing at screening
Download the FY2027 versions of the forms from the Application Guidelines page rather than reusing an old FORM2
The doctoral degree certificate is not required at application, but an original copy must reach JSPS before the fellowship starting date
If several candidates apply through the same host researcher, priorities must be set - confirm yours is the one submitted
alerts: Two fixed rounds a year: FY2027 2nd deadline 23 April 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results early August 2027, arrival 1 September - 30 November 2027; the FY2027 1st round closed 28 August 2026
Outbound airfare and the settling-in allowance are withheld if you already have a mailing address in Japan before the fellowship start date
Each host researcher may submit up to three applications, and only 120 fellowships are awarded per recruitment, so the strength of the host-candidate research plan decides the outcome
From FY2024 applications, award letters and related documents for successful candidates are sent to host institutions, not directly to fellows
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The candidate sends FORM2 and the recommendation letter to the host researcher, who enters everything on the Japanese-language JSPS Electronic Application System and the host institution transmits it to the president of JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the deadline day.
